1.title: Are the new US tariffs a big threat?
1.text: Faisal Islam is a BBC editor. He says the new US tariffs are less of a threat. They are not like last April, when the news shocked the world. Now the US talks about more negotiations. The tariffs will not start until January or February. The rates are top limits, and countries can negotiate them.

2.title: Why Trump's new tariffs are less of a threat
2.text:
BBC economics editor Faisal Islam says this week's tariff announcement feels different from last April. There was no big show, and the US now talks about more negotiations. In his view, the goal is to give the old tariffs a stronger legal base.

The tariffs will not start until January or February, after a period of talks. The rates announced are upper limits, and countries can negotiate them. The Supreme Court ended the original emergency tariffs earlier this year.

Islam also says the world has changed its trade routes. China's exports to the US have fallen, but its sales to other countries have grown much more. Democrats, who will have more power in Congress, want to repeal the tariffs.

3.title: Faisal Islam: Why Trump's new tariffs are less of a threat
3.text:
Writing for the BBC, Faisal Islam argues that this week's tariff announcement is much less dramatic than last April's. There was no Rose Garden event, and officials spoke of broad negotiations over excess capacity. Around the world, he says, the view is that the move is an attempt to strengthen the legal basis of the tariffs rather than a change in the trade agenda.

The tariffs are not due until January or February, after a consultation, and the rates announced are ceilings that can be negotiated. The Supreme Court struck down the original emergency basis earlier this year, so many countries now face two legal bases. A group of 25 states is suing to strike down the forced labour tariffs.

Islam notes that the rest of the world has rerouted trade around the US. China's exports in 2026 are down about 8% from 2024, but increased sales elsewhere more than make up for it. Hakeem Jeffries, the Speaker-designate, said the new House would move to repeal the tariffs in its first 100 days.
